label: Unique Population Registry Code
native_label: Clave Única de Registro de Población (CURP)
structure: 18 characters, no separators: 1 initial of first surname + 2 first internal vowel of first surname + 3 initial of second surname + 4 first letter of given name + 5-10 YYMMDD birth date + 11 sex (H hombre, M mujer) + 12-13 state of birth (2 letters, NE = born abroad) + 14 first internal consonant of first surname + 15 of second surname + 16 of given name + 17 homonymy-and-century character (0-9 for births to 1999-12-31, A-J for births from 2000-01-01) + 18 check digit (0-9). Name rules (RENAPO Reglas 2021 s.5): Ñ -> X in positions 1-4 and 14-16; special characters (/ - . ') -> X; leading particles DA DAS DE DEL DER DI DIE DD EL LA LAS LE LES LOS MAC MC VAN VON Y skipped; first given name MARIA, MA., MA, M., M, JOSE, J., J skipped when a second given name exists; no internal vowel/consonant -> X; one surname -> X in positions 3 and 15; no surnames -> XXX and XX; positions 1-4 forming a word in Anexo 01 'Catálogo de palabras altisonantes' -> second letter replaced by X (e.g. OFELIA PEDRERO DOMINGUEZ -> PXDO)
encodes: names (initials and internal letters), date of birth, sex, place (state of birth, or abroad), century (via position 17), homonymy sequence
check: RENAPO says only that position 18 is a digit from 'an algorithm' (not published). Reference algorithm (python-stdnum; agrees with Wikipedia's example): value of each of the first 17 characters in the alphabet 0-9 A-N Ñ O-Z (0=0 ... 9=9, A=10 ... N=23, Ñ=24, O=25 ... Z=36), weights 18, 17, ..., 2 for positions 1-17, check = (10 - sum mod 10) mod 10
examples: BOXW310820HNERXN09 (python-stdnum doctest: male, born 1931-08-20 abroad) ; SABC560626MDFLRN01 (computed from RENAPO's illustrative case 'Concepción Salgado Briseño, born 1956-06-26 in the Distrito Federal', Instructivo Normativo, DOF 2018-06-18; the official figure prints SABC560626MDFLRN09, whose last digit fails the reference algorithm — illustrative only) ; invalid: BOXW310820HNERXN08 (stdnum)
assigned: at birth registration with the Registro Civil or a consular office (Reglas 2021 s.6); CURP introduced by the Acuerdo of 1996-10-23 (DOF), so older people received it later on application; temporary CURP for foreigners (180/365 days)
place_codes: Anexo 03 'Catálogo de Entidades Federativas para la conformación de la CURP' of RENAPO's Reglas (2021): 32 states + NE; not attached to the public PDF; python-stdnum holds the 33 codes (AS BC BS CC CH CL CM CS DF DG GR GT HG JC MC MN MS NE NL NT OC PL QR QT SL SP SR TC TL TS VZ YN ZS). Licence: Mexican official administrative texts are excluded from copyright (LFDA art. 14 fr. VIII — not re-verified). Wikidata property: not checked
from_until: from 1996-10-23 (Acuerdo, DOF); current rules: Instructivo Normativo DOF 2018-06-18, modified DOF 2021-10-18, RENAPO Reglas 2021-10-22. CDMX is still coded DF
sources: https://sidof.segob.gob.mx/notas/docFuente/5526717 (Instructivo Normativo 2018, position table) ; https://www.gob.mx/cms/uploads/attachment/file/681698/reglas_para_la_ejecucion_de_los_procedimientos_asignacion_de_la_curp.pdf (Reglas 2021, name rules s.5, positions 17-18) ; https://arthurdejong.org/python-stdnum/doc/2.1/stdnum.mx.curp (check algorithm, reference) ; https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clave_%C3%9Anica_de_Registro_de_Poblaci%C3%B3n
design_claims: encodes names, date, sex, state of birth: confirmed (issuer) ; check 'weighted mod 10': confirmed at reference level only (RENAPO does not publish the algorithm; stdnum's version reproduces Wikipedia's example) ; RENAPO's list of inconvenient words: corrected: it is Anexo 01 'Catálogo de palabras altisonantes' of RENAPO's Reglas (2021), listed in the PDF but not attached; no issuer copy found; python-stdnum carries an 81-word list (LGPL code — the words are facts, but cite and re-derive rather than copy the file) ; replacement by X: confirmed, it is the second letter that becomes X (PEDRERO DOMINGUEZ OFELIA -> PXDO) ; particles DE, DEL, LA skipped: confirmed, full list of 19 particles plus the MARIA/JOSE first-name rule ; Ñ written as X: confirmed (positions 1-4 and 14-16) ; homonymy digit: corrected: position 17 is 0-9 for births to 1999 and A-J (not A-Z) from 2000, and it is the first value (0 or A) unless the first 16 characters collide
notes: Own check verified: BOXW310820HNERXN09 pass; SABC560626MDFLRN0 + computed 1 (official figure shows 9, fails); Wikipedia's example (a named person, not recorded here) passes. Reglas 1.4 and 1.6 conflict on diaeresis (1.4: X, 1.6: Ü -> U with example ARGÜELLO -> AUPD); use U. Compound surnames use the first word. Foreigners get CURP with NE and temporary CURPs (out of scope)

label: MyKad identity card number (NRIC)
structure: YYMMDD (birth date, no century) + '-' + PB (2-digit birthplace code: state, or country/region for births abroad) + '-' + NNN (serial) + S (last digit: odd = male, even = female); display 770305-02-1234, electronic 12 digits
encodes: date (no century), place (state of birth, or country/region of birth abroad), sex
check: none
examples: 770305-02-1234 (python-stdnum doctest; born 1977-03-05, Kedah, even = female) ; invalid: 771305-02-1234 (month 13) ; invalid: 770305-17-1234 (code 17 unassigned) ; also 900101-14-5678 (press example, Kuala Lumpur)
assigned: at birth registration (the birth certificate carries the number); MyKid card at birth, MyKad at 12
place_codes: JPN publishes both lists. States (https://www.jpn.gov.my/kod-negeri/): 01/21-24 Johor, 02/25-27 Kedah, 03/28-29 Kelantan, 04/30 Melaka, 05/31/59 Negeri Sembilan, 06/32-33 Pahang, 07/34-35 Pulau Pinang, 08/36-39 Perak, 09/40 Perlis, 10/41-44 Selangor, 11/45-46 Terengganu, 12/47-49 Sabah, 13/50-53 Sarawak, 14/54-57 WP Kuala Lumpur, 15/58 WP Labuan, 16 WP Putrajaya, 82 state unknown. Abroad (https://www.jpn.gov.my/kod-negara/, 294 rows): 60 Brunei, 61 Indonesia, 62 Cambodia, 63 Laos, 64 Myanmar, 65 Philippines, 66 Singapore, 67 Thailand, 68 Vietnam, 71/72 abroad (luar negara), 74 China, 75 India, 76 Pakistan, 77 Saudi Arabia, 78 Sri Lanka, 79 Bangladesh, 83 Asia-Pacific/Oceania, 84 South America, 85 Africa, 86 Europe, 87 Britain/Ireland, 88 Middle East, 89 Far East (Japan, Korea, Taiwan), 90 Caribbean/Central America, 91 North America, 92 Eastern Europe/USSR, 93 others, 98 stateless, 99 refugee/unspecified/Mecca. Government web page, no licence stated; small enough to curate. Not on Wikidata
from_until: 12-digit format since 1991 (with the computerised IC; MyKad from 2001 keeps it); older 7-digit IC numbers out of scope
sources: https://www.jpn.gov.my/kod-negeri/ ; https://www.jpn.gov.my/kod-negara/ ; https://arthurdejong.org/python-stdnum/doc/stdnum.my.nric ; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malaysian_identity_card
design_claims: encodes date, birthplace (state or country), sex: confirmed ; check none: confirmed ; birthplace codes with source: confirmed: JPN's Kod Negeri and Kod Negara pages (issuer) ; unassigned place code exists: confirmed: 00, 17-20, 69, 70, 73, 80, 81, 94-97 appear in neither JPN list (stdnum also rejects 17)
notes: Use 17-20 for safe numbers (stdnum names 17 as 'unknown birth place'). Draw states from both the original codes (01-16) and the later extra codes per state; JPN does not say when each extra code is used, so weight them only if a source turns up. Code 82 'state unknown' is assigned, not safe. The 1991 start date is from my knowledge of the Wikipedia article, not re-verified here. The structure (date + code + serial + odd/even sex) is issuer-level only through JPN's code pages and press quotes; stdnum and Wikipedia agree.

label: Citizen service number
structure: 9 digits s0..s8 (8-digit numbers are padded with a leading zero), no internal meaning; numerically identical to the former sofinummer. Display often 9 digits or 'NNNN.NN.NNN'.
encodes: nothing
check: elfproef: 9*s0 + 8*s1 + 7*s2 + 6*s3 + 5*s4 + 4*s5 + 3*s6 + 2*s7 + (-1)*s8 must be divisible by 11 (RvIG Logisch Ontwerp BSN)
examples: 999900006 and 999900110 (test BSNs in the SBV-Z XIS test set handbook, per a search excerpt; the PDF returned 404 when fetched) ; no authority-published worked example found in the Logisch Ontwerp BSN
assigned: at birth registration in the BRP (municipality), or on registration as resident/non-resident (RNI); BSN replaced the sofinummer in 2007
from_until: BSN since 2007-11-26 (Wet algemene bepalingen burgerservicenummer), numerically the sofinummer series; unchanged
sources: https://www.rvig.nl/sites/default/files/2023-12/Logisch%20Ontwerp%20BSN%202024.Q1.pdf (element Burgerservicenummer: length 8..9, elfproef as above) ; https://arthurdejong.org/python-stdnum/doc/stdnum.nl.bsn
design_claims: nothing; 11-proef; wrong check: confirmed
notes: Test BSNs exist: RvIG runs a GBA-V/BV BSN test environment ('proefomgeving') with a test dataset of persons (Testdataset persoonslijsten proefomgevingen GBA-V.ods on rvig.nl, contents not read), and SBV-Z/CIBG hand out test BSNs (seen beginning 9999...). No source was found that says a BSN range is reserved and never issued, so test_numbers/reserved_range is not claimed. Examples checked with a script: 999900006 and 999900110 pass the elfproef; 123456789 fails. The BSN space is dense, so wrong check is right.

label: National identity number (birth number)
structure: DDMMYY (birth date) + III (individnummer; last digit even = female, odd = male) + K1 + K2 (two mod-11 check digits); 11 digits, no separator (often shown DDMMYY III KK). Century from the individual number: 749-500 born 1854-1899, 499-000 born 1900-1999, 999-900 also born 1940-1999, 999-500 born 2000-2039; each series used in descending order. D-number: day + 40. Synthetic (test) numbers: month + 80 (dd8Myy / dd9Myy). From 2032: new numbers no longer encode century or sex, and K1 may take up to four values.
encodes: date, sex (until 2032), century (individual-number range, until 2032)
check: K1 = 11 - (3,7,6,1,8,9,4,5,2 · d1..i3 mod 11), 11 -> 0, 10 -> number rejected; K2 = 11 - (5,4,3,2,7,6,5,4,3,2 · d1..K1 mod 11), 11 -> 0, 10 -> rejected. Validation form: weighted sum including the check digit with weight 1 must be 0 mod 11. 2032 rule: the remainder for K1 may be 0, 1, 2 or 3 (K1 = {11,12,13,14} - r, minus 11 if > 10, 10 rejected); K2 unchanged.
examples: 02013299997 (born 2032-01-02, individnummer 999, k1 9, k2 7; Skatteetaten worked example, valid under old and new rule) ; 30108299920 (born 1982-10-30, individnummer 999, k1 2, k2 0) ; 30108299939 (born 1982-10-30, same individnummer, valid only under the 2032 k1 rule, remainder 1)
assigned: at birth registration in Folkeregisteret, or when a person settles in Norway (D-number for temporary residents); fødselsnummer system since 1964
safe_source: https://skatteetaten.github.io/folkeregisteret-api-dokumentasjon/dokumenter/foedselsEllerDNummerValidator.js (Skatteetaten's validator: synthetic numbers must have month digit 8 or 9, i.e. month + 80) ; https://www.skatteetaten.no/deling/folkeregisteret/pid/validering/ ; https://www.skatteetaten.no/en/testdata/ (Tenor synthetic test population)
from_until: 1964 format (century in individual number, sex in 9th digit, single-valued K1) for all numbers assigned up to 2031; from 2032 new numbers (also for persons born before 2032) are gender-neutral, do not encode century, and use the extended K1 rule; existing numbers are kept
sources: https://www.skatteetaten.no/rettskilder/type/handboker/folkeregisterhandboken/gjeldende/kapittel2-registreringspliktige-personer-identifikasjonsnummer/ID-2-2.001/ID-2-2.006/ ; https://skatteetaten.github.io/folkeregisteret-api-dokumentasjon/nytt-fodselsnummer-fra-2032/ ; https://snl.no/fødselsnummer
design_claims: synthetic test numbers with month + 80 as the safe method: confirmed (Skatteetaten's own validator accepts synthetic numbers only as dd8Myy/dd9Myy and subtracts 80 from the month; the NHN SyntPop forum slides of Oct 2023 also say Skatteetaten test persons are month + 80, while Persontjenesten test persons use month + 65) ; 'Skatteverket-like' is loose: Skatteetaten publishes a construction rule and a searchable synthetic population (Tenor, ID-porten login), not a downloadable list ; 'century (individual range)': confirmed until 2032, corrected for numbers assigned from 2032 (no century, no sex)
notes: Safe numbers = valid K1/K2 over a date with month + 80; these never belong to a real person but may coincide with a Tenor synthetic test person, which is the intended use. A month + 80 number fails validators that check the calendar date, so testers should know which validators accept synthetic numbers. Design must add the 2032 rule: from 2032 the library should not encode sex (and should not imply century) for persons assigned a number on or after 2032-01-01, and must use the multi-valued K1 for those. Examples checked with a script: 02013299997 pass old+new, 30108299920 pass old+new, 30108299939 fails old / passes new (as the source says), 30108299938 (altered) fails. D-numbers (day + 40) and H-numbers out of scope.

label: IRD number
native_label: IRD number / tau IRD (Te Tari Taake)
structure: NNNNNNN or NNNNNNNN (7 or 8 digit base, padded to 8 with a leading 0 for the check) + C (check). Display NN-NNN-NNN or NNN-NNN-NNN, electronic 8-9 digits. Validators accept only 10,000,000-150,000,000 (the range issued or expected to be issued, per the IRD specification as quoted by validators)
encodes: nothing
check: mod 11 with two weight sets: base (8 digits) times 3,2,7,6,5,4,3,2; r = sum mod 11; C = 0 if r = 0 else 11 - r; if C = 10, recompute with weights 7,4,3,2,5,2,7,6 and the same reduction; if that also gives 10 the number is invalid (implementations differ on this last step)
examples: 49-091-850 (python-stdnum) ; 49-098-576 (python-stdnum) ; invalid: 136-410-133 (stdnum). No IRD worked example retrieved
assigned: on application to Inland Revenue, at any age (children commonly at birth registration via the 'Smart Start' option — not verified this session)
from_until: 8-digit numbers older, 9-digit (>= 100,000,000) issued later; start dates not found
sources: https://www.ird.govt.nz/-/media/Project/IR/PDF/2020RWTNRWTSpecificationDocumentv10.pdf (IRD specification cited by stdnum; now 404) ; https://arthurdejong.org/python-stdnum/doc/stdnum.nz.ird ; https://www.npmjs.com/package/@fnzc/nz-ird-validator (cites IRD 'NRWT and RWT Specification Document' of 2016-03-31) ; https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/financials/24c/faitx/new-zealand.html
design_claims: encodes nothing: confirmed ; mod 11, two weight sets: confirmed (reference: stdnum, fnzc validator and Oracle, all citing the IRD RWT/NRWT specification; the IRD PDF itself returned 404 and was not read) ; safe = wrong check: confirmed
notes: Own check: 49091850 pass, 49098576 pass, 136410133 fail (computed 2). Draw bases in 10,000,000-150,000,000 only; skip bases whose primary and secondary checks both give 10. Numbers above 150,000,000 are rejected by validators but not documented as never issued, so not used as a reserved range

label: National Identity Document number (Unique Identification Code)
native_label: Documento Nacional de Identidad (DNI) / Código Único de Identificación (CUI)
structure: SS (series, first two digits) + NNNNNN (6 digits) = 8-digit CUI, printed on the DNI followed by '-' and one check character (digit, or letter in the alternative form). Display NNNNNNNN-C, electronic 8 digits (the check character is usually not stored or asked for). Series 1984-1996: first two digits = department or province of registration (people born up to August 1978); from 1996: national series, e.g. 40-49 born from September 1978 to the early 1990s, 70-78 born about 1992-2003, 60-63, 81, 90-91 born from 2002, 80 nationwide (es.wikipedia, uncited)
encodes: place (department/province of registration) for numbers issued 1984-1996; from 1996 the series follows birth period (sequence); nothing else
check: not published by RENIEC. Reference algorithm (python-stdnum only): weights 3,2,7,6,5,4,3,2 over the 8 digits, c = sum mod 11; check digit = 6,5,4,3,2,1,1,0,9,8,7 for c = 0..10, or check letter = K,J,I,H,G,F,E,D,C,B,A for c = 0..10
examples: 10117410-2 (python-stdnum; sum 70, c = 4 -> 2 or G) ; invalid: 10117410-3 (stdnum). No second published example found
assigned: for adults at first DNI (from 1984/1996); minors registered from the 2000s, in some cases from birth (CUI on the birth record) — es.wikipedia
place_codes: 1984-1996 series-to-department list on es.wikipedia (uncited); not needed if the generator draws only post-1996 series
from_until: geographic series 1984-1996 (still held by people born up to August 1978); national series from 1996; electronic DNI 2013 and DNI 3.0 in 2025 keep the number
sources: https://arthurdejong.org/python-stdnum/doc/2.1/stdnum.pe.cui ; https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Documento_Nacional_de_Identidad_(Per%C3%BA) ; https://larepublica.pe/sociedad/2025/02/22/este-es-el-verdadero-significado-del-ultimo-digito-del-dni-y-en-que-casos-es-utilizado-por-los-peruanos-segun-reniec-atmp-392304 ; https://www.gob.pe/235-documento-nacional-de-identidad-dni
design_claims: PE DNI encodes nothing (survey): corrected: numbers issued 1984-1996 carry the department/province of registration in the first two digits, and the post-1996 national series follow birth period (es.wikipedia, uncited); for a person born after 1978 the number is effectively a birth-period sequence ; check character (survey): partly confirmed: the DNI prints a check character after the 8 digits (La República 2022, 2025 citing RENIEC: generated by an algorithm, not the number of namesakes); RENIEC does not publish the algorithm; python-stdnum's weights 3,2,7,6,5,4,3,2 mod 11 with a digit or letter table is the only source found (evidence single) ; safe = wrong check: confirmed, but note that most consumers validate only the 8 digits, which have no check, so a wrong check character protects only when the 9th character is emitted
notes: Own check verified: 10117410 -> c 4 -> '2' (pass), '3' fails. The 9th character is optional in practice; the RUC for a natural person is 10 + DNI + RUC check (stdnum.pe.ruc). Series table needs a better source before the generator uses birth-period series; drawing a uniform 8-digit number in the 40-78 series is the simple option. Foreign residents use the carné de extranjería (out of scope)

label: Computerised National Identity Card number
structure: P (province: 1 Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, 2 FATA (merged into KP 2018), 3 Punjab, 4 Sindh, 5 Balochistan, 6 Islamabad, 7 Gilgit-Baltistan, 8 Azad Kashmir) + D (division within the province) + LLL (district / tehsil / union council; sources disagree on the split) + '-' + NNNNNNN (7-digit family/serial number) + '-' + S (sex: odd = male, even = female); display 34201-0891231-8, electronic 13 digits
encodes: place (locality of registration / residence at registration), sex
check: none
examples: 34201-0891231-8 (python-stdnum doctest; Punjab, even last digit = female) ; 42201-0397640-8 (python-stdnum doctest; Sindh, Karachi division 42, female) ; no authority-published example found
assigned: CNIC at 18; children are registered earlier (CRC / B-Form) with a 13-digit number of the same shape that carries over to the CNIC (per NADRA practice; not verified in this survey)
place_codes: No official NADRA list of the 5-digit locality codes found. Province digits 1-8 and two-digit division codes (e.g. 11 Bannu, 13 Hazara, 35 Lahore, 42 Karachi, 54 Quetta, 61 Islamabad, 71 Gilgit-Baltistan, 81 Mirpur, 82 Muzaffarabad) are listed on Wikipedia without a cited source; digits 3-5 have no published list. Not on Wikidata
from_until: 13-digit CNIC since 2000 (NADRA); earlier manual NIC numbers (11 digits) out of scope
sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CNIC_(Pakistan) ; https://arthurdejong.org/python-stdnum/doc/stdnum.pk.cnic ; https://tribune.com.pk/story/1403682/theres-cnic-number-know
design_claims: encodes province and locality, sex: confirmed (reference) ; check none: confirmed ; province/division/district code list: unconfirmed: no official list published; only province digits and some division codes on Wikipedia ; unassigned locality code: corrected: no locality list exists to pick from, so use an unassigned province digit (0 or 9: no province uses them in any source) as the safe method ; sex in the last digit: confirmed (odd male, even female)
notes: stdnum validates only length, format and the province digit; a first digit 0 or 9 fails stdnum (unknown province), which is the cost of the only place-based safe method available. Realistic numbers: draw province by population, then the division from Wikipedia's list where available, digits 3-5 random. Gender 'X' (transgender) on the card is not encoded in the number as far as sources say. The 2000 start date is from my general knowledge of NADRA, not verified here. ; [merge 2026-11-04] Safe: province digit 0 or 9 (no locality list is published).

label: PESEL number
structure: YYMMDD (birth date; month + century offset: 1800-1899 +80, 1900-1999 +0, 2000-2099 +20, 2100-2199 +40, 2200-2299 +60) + NNN (serial, digits 7-9) + S (digit 10, serial continued: even incl. 0 = female, odd = male) + C (check). 11 digits, no separators in display or electronic form
encodes: date, sex, century (month offset)
check: weights 1-3-7-9-1-3-7-9-1-3 on digits 1-10; C = (10 - (sum mod 10)) mod 10, i.e. units digit of sum 0 gives C = 0
examples: 02070803628 (female born 1902-07-08; OECD/Ministry of Finance worked example)
assigned: at birth registration (ex officio on entry into the PESEL register, ustawa o ewidencji ludnosci art. 15-16); foreigners only with listed residence or protection statuses (art. 7)
from_until: PESEL register since 1979 (OECD doc says the register operates since 1977); current statutory basis ustawa z 24 IX 2010 (in force 2012), check-digit rule formalised by rozporzadzenie MSW of 4 I 2012 (Dz.U. 2012 poz. 74, in force 2013-01-01); format unchanged
sources: https://api.sejm.gov.pl/eli/acts/DU/2010/1427/text.html (art. 15 ust. 2: structure, +80/+0/+20, sex digit) ; https://api.sejm.gov.pl/eli/acts/DU/2012/74/text.html (par. 7: weights and check rule) ; https://www.oecd.org/content/dam/oecd/en/topics/policy-issue-focus/aeoi/poland-tin.pdf (adds +40/+60) ; https://pl.wikipedia.org/wiki/PESEL
design_claims: encodes date, sex, century (month offset): confirmed ; check weights 1-3-7-9: confirmed ; safe = wrong check: confirmed (no official test PESEL range found; only an NFZ e-prescription test-environment notice, not a published range)
notes: Examples verified with own script: 02070803628 passes. Also passing (non-official): stdnum doctest 44051401359 and pl.wikipedia 55030101193 and 55030101230 (sum units 0 -> check 0); 44051401358 fails as expected. The law (art. 15) lists only the 1800-2099 offsets; +40/+60 come from the Ministry's OECD sheet. Searched for official test PESEL numbers: none found. A number is never reassigned to another person (art. 22). Foreigners (incl. UKR-status refugees since 2022) get the same format, out of scope.

label: Tax identification number
structure: 9 digits: first 8 sequential (first digit = range: 1 and 2 historically for individuals, 3 for individuals from mid-2019; 45 non-resident individuals; 5, 6, 7, 8, 9 legal entities and special cases) + 1 check digit. Display 123 456 789.
encodes: nothing (the first digit gives the type of holder and, for individuals, roughly the period of assignment)
check: weights 9,8,7,6,5,4,3,2 over the first 8 digits; r = sum mod 11; check = 0 if r is 0 or 1, else 11 - r. Not published in the law (Decreto-Lei 14/2013 arts. 4-5 only say 'last digit is a check digit'); python-stdnum and simula.pt agree.
examples: 501964843 (legal entity, python-stdnum doctest; invalid variant 501964842) ; no published individual (range 1/2/3) example found
assigned: on request to the Autoridade Tributária (often at birth via the 'Nascer Cidadão' process or when the Cartão de Cidadão is first issued); any age
from_until: NIF since 1986 (Decreto-Lei 463/79 / 14/2013 regime); range 2 for individuals until mid-2019, range 3 from June/July 2019 (AT notice of 2019-04-08)
sources: https://info.portaldasfinancas.gov.pt/pt/destaques/Paginas/Atribuicao_Nova_Gama_de_NIF_a_Pessoas_Singulares.aspx (AT: nine digits, first eight sequential, last a check digit; range 2 then range 3) ; https://simula.pt/simuladores/simulador_validar_nif_iban ; https://arthurdejong.org/python-stdnum/doc/stdnum.pt.nif
design_claims: nothing; mod 11; wrong check: confirmed (structure at issuer level, the mod-11 rule at reference level)
notes: Generation should pick the first digit by assignment date: 1 for the oldest numbers, 2 for most adults, 3 for numbers assigned from mid-2019 (children, new immigrants). Example check: 501964843 passes, 501964842 fails. The Cartão de Cidadão's civil identification number (NIC) is a different number with its own check; out of scope for 1.0.

label: personal numeric code
structure: S (sex and century: 1/2 = male/female born 1900-1999, 3/4 = 1800-1899, 5/6 = 2000-2099, 7/8 = male/female foreign residents, century not encoded) + YYMMDD (birth date) + JJ (county or Bucharest sector code; 70 for all CNPs generated in the Integrated Information System from 2024-05-08) + NNN (serial 001-999 per assignment point) + C (check). 13 digits, written as one block (format SAALLZZJJNNNC)
encodes: sex, century, date, place (county or sector of birth, or of domicile/residence when the CNP was assigned; no place for CNPs generated from 2024-05-08 with JJ = 70)
check: weights 2 7 9 1 4 6 3 5 8 2 7 9 on digits 1-12; r = sum mod 11; C = r, except r = 10 gives C = 1
examples: 1630615123457 (male born 1963-06-15, county 12 Cluj, serial 345; python-stdnum doctest, not authority) ; invalid: 1630615123458 (wrong check). The ANAF/OECD sheet's sample 1010100012345 is a placeholder and fails the check
assigned: at birth registration (civil status registration); foreign residents get one from the General Inspectorate for Immigration on their residence permit
place_codes: County/sector codes: 01-39 counties (alphabetical with exceptions), 40 Bucuresti, 41-46 Bucuresti sectors 1-6, 47-48 sectors 7-8 (abolished), 51 Calarasi, 52 Giurgiu, 70 any (from 2024); ANAF's OECD sheet also allows 80-83 (meaning not published). Listed in ro.wikipedia citing the HG 1375/2006 methodological norms (art. 14-15); legal text, so no licence restriction expected. No Wikidata property found for the CNP county code (counties carry SIRUTA P843, a different code)
from_until: CNP mandatory from Decret 59/1978 (2 March 1978); structure per HG 1375/2006 norms; from 2024-05-08 (SIIASC rollout, unit by unit) new CNPs use JJ = 70; existing CNPs unchanged
sources: https://www.oecd.org/content/dam/oecd/en/topics/policy-issue-focus/aeoi/romania-tin.pdf (ANAF: S digits 1-8, YYMMDD, JJ ranges) ; https://ro.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cod_numeric_personal_(Rom%C3%A2nia) (check weights, r=10 -> 1, JJ list, 70) ; https://www.bzi.ro/se-schimba-cnp-urile-romanilor-ce-trebuie-sa-stie-cetatenii-4981249 (DGEP head on JJ = 70 from 2024-05-08)
design_claims: encodes date, sex, century, county: confirmed (county is birth or residence at assignment; replaced by 70 from 2024-05-08) ; weights 279146358279: confirmed (r = 10 -> C = 1) ; 2024+ changes: corrected: the 2024 change is the county code 70 for new CNPs, not new sex digits; 7/8 are foreign residents (since HG 1251/2006 asylum norms), and no source gives a CNP digit 9 (a leading 9 is ANAF's NIF for non-residents, a different number) ; safe = wrong check: confirmed
notes: Examples verified with own script: 1630615123457 passes, 1630615123458 fails, ANAF placeholder 1010100012345 fails (placeholder). Structure is at issuer level (ANAF via OECD), the check rule only at reference level (ro.wikipedia + python-stdnum); HG 1375/2006 text not fetched. Generator: births before 2024-05-08 draw JJ from the county list (by birthplace); births from 2024-05-08 should use JJ = 70 (rollout was gradual: about 50 of 3,188 units connected at first, so a mix is realistic). Foreigners (7/8) out of scope.

label: unique master citizen number
structure: DD (day) + MM (month) + GGG (last three digits of birth year: 9xx = 19xx, 0xx = 20xx) + RR (registration area) + BBB (serial for people born the same day: 000-499 male, 500-999 female) + K (check). 13 digits, one block
encodes: date, sex, century (3-digit year), place (registration area of the birth-register entry; 70 for citizens registered at a consular post abroad)
check: modulo 11 (the law names the method only). Algorithm as in the Slovenian Uredba 1999 and sr.wikipedia: weights 7 6 5 4 3 2 7 6 5 4 3 2 on digits 1-12; r = sum mod 11; K = 11 - r; r = 0 gives K = 0; r = 1 is never assigned (serial skipped)
examples: 2902932505526 (Slovenian Uredba 1999 worked example, RR 50: algorithm only) ; 0101006500006 (en.wikipedia, RR 50: algorithm only)
assigned: after birth registration: the registrar sends the birth extract within 15 days and the Ministry of Internal Affairs determines the number (Zakon o JMBG 2018, art. 3, 6, 7); the RR follows the place of the birth-register entry
place_codes: Zakon o jedinstvenom maticnom broju gradjana (Sl. glasnik RS 24/2018) art. 5 lists, per local self-government unit: 70 abroad (consular), 71 Beograd, 72 Sumadija/Pomoravlje (Arandjelovac, Jagodina...), 73 Nis area, 74 South Morava (Leskovac, Vranje...), 75 Zajecar/Bor, 76 Podunavlje/Branicevo, 77 Podrinje/Kolubara, 78 Kraljevo/Rasina/Raska, 79 Uzice/Moravica, 80 Novi Sad, 81 Sombor, 82 Subotica, 83 Becej/Srbobran, 84 Kikinda, 85 Zrenjanin, 86 Pancevo, 87 Vrsac, 88 Ruma/Indjija, 89 Sremska Mitrovica, 91-97 Kosovo and Metohija. 27 codes, statute (public text, no licence issue). No Wikidata property found
from_until: JMBG from 1977-01-08 (Sl. list SFRJ 58/1976); current Serbian law Sl. glasnik RS 24/2018 (in force 8 days after publication, 2018), numbers assigned earlier keep their RR
sources: https://www.paragraf.rs/propisi/zakon-o-jedinstvenom-maticnom-broju-gradjana.html (art. 4 structure, art. 5 areas, art. 6 modulo 11) ; https://sr.wikipedia.org/sr-el/Jedinstveni_mati%C4%8Dni_broj_gra%C4%91ana (weights, r = 1 skip) ; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unique_Master_Citizen_Number
design_claims: encodes date, sex, region: confirmed (region = registration area of the birth-register entry, by municipality) ; mod 11: confirmed (law says modulo 11; weights from the shared SFRJ algorithm at reference level) ; RR source: issuer (law 24/2018 art. 5) ; 10/11 case: r = 0 -> K = 0, r = 1 not assigned (sr.wikipedia, Slovenian Uredba); en.wikipedia's 'm = 10 or 11 -> 0' is a looser validator rule ; safe = wrong check: confirmed
notes: No authority-published worked example with this country code found. The algorithm is the shared SFRJ one; the Slovenian Uredba example 2902932505526 and 0101006500006 (RR 50) verify it. Structure and RR list issuer-level, weights reference-level (sr.wikipedia + en.wikipedia + Slovenian Uredba). The 2018 law does not use the codes 90, 98, 99; Kosovo (XK) issues its own personal numbers since 2000s, out of scope. Foreigners: separate number for foreigners (old codes 06, 66), out of scope. python-stdnum has no Serbian JMBG module (only rs.pib).

label: taxpayer identification number (individual)
structure: NNNN (code of the tax authority that assigned it: first 2 digits = region (federal subject) code, next 2 = local inspectorate) + XXXXXX (serial in that authority's section of the taxpayer register) + C1 C2 (check digits). 12 digits for individuals (10 for organisations, out of scope)
encodes: place (region and tax office where the INN was assigned: residence at assignment), sequence
examples: 123456789047 (python-stdnum doctest, illustrative, not authority) ; invalid: 123456789037. No authority-published worked example found
assigned: on registration with the tax authority at the place of residence (on application, or ex officio when tax accounting needs it, Tax Code art. 84); ru.wikipedia says people born from 1999 get one from ZAGS data (not verified). Not every person holds one
place_codes: Tax authority codes (SOUN directory) are published by the FNS (nalog.ru, open data); the first two digits follow the federal subject codes (85+ subjects). Licence of FNS open data not checked. No Wikidata property found
from_until: INN for individuals from 1999 (Tax Code art. 84); assignment rules Prikaz FNS 29.06.2012 MMV-7-6/435@; format unchanged
sources: https://www.oecd.org/content/dam/oecd/en/topics/policy-issue-focus/aeoi/russia-tin.pdf (FNS: NNNN tax authority code + 6-digit serial + 2 control digits, 'algorithm set by the FNS') ; https://ru.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D0%98%D0%B4%D0%B5%D0%BD%D1%82%D0%B8%D1%84%D0%B8%D0%BA%D0%B0%D1%86%D0%B8%D0%BE%D0%BD%D0%BD%D1%8B%D0%B9_%D0%BD%D0%BE%D0%BC%D0%B5%D1%80_%D0%BD%D0%B0%D0%BB%D0%BE%D0%B3%D0%BE%D0%BF%D0%BB%D0%B0%D1%82%D0%B5%D0%BB%D1%8C%D1%89%D0%B8%D0%BA%D0%B0 (weights) ; python-stdnum stdnum/ru/inn.py
design_claims: INN encodes region: confirmed (region and tax office of assignment, i.e. residence at assignment, not birthplace) ; weighted mod 11: confirmed (two passes, mod 11 mod 10) ; safe = wrong check: confirmed
notes: Example verified with own script: 123456789047 passes, 123456789037 fails. Structure is issuer-level (FNS via OECD), the weights reference-level. Generator: region code from residence (federal subject code) plus a real inspectorate number would need the SOUN list; without it, use code NN + 01..NN is a guess, so prefer real codes. Only persons who registered hold an INN, so make it optional or assign at an adult age.

label: individual insurance account number
structure: NNN-NNN-NNN (9-digit insurance number, issued without meaning) + CC (2-digit control number). Display form NNN-NNN-NNN CC, electronic form 11 digits
encodes: nothing
check: S = sum of digit x position counted from the end (weights 9 8 7 6 5 4 3 2 1); S < 100 gives CC = S; S = 100 or 101 gives 00; S > 101 gives S mod 101, and a result of 100 gives 00. The check applies only to numbers greater than 001-001-998
examples: 112-233-445 95 (worked example in the PFR rule as reproduced by Business::PFR: sum 95) ; invalid: 112-233-445 96. Only one example found
assigned: since 2020-07-15 automatically on birth registration (from the ZAGS record); older people at first employment or on request (ru.wikipedia)
from_until: individual (personified) accounting from 1996 (law 27-FZ of 1996-04-01); automatic assignment at birth from 2020-07-15; format unchanged. Numbers up to 001-001-998 are exempt from the check
sources: https://metacpan.org/pod/Business::PFR (algorithm text from the PFR verification rules) ; https://ru.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D0%A1%D1%82%D1%80%D0%B0%D1%85%D0%BE%D0%B2%D0%BE%D0%B9_%D0%BD%D0%BE%D0%BC%D0%B5%D1%80_%D0%B8%D0%BD%D0%B4%D0%B8%D0%B2%D0%B8%D0%B4%D1%83%D0%B0%D0%BB%D1%8C%D0%BD%D0%BE%D0%B3%D0%BE_%D0%BB%D0%B8%D1%86%D0%B5%D0%B2%D0%BE%D0%B3%D0%BE_%D1%81%D1%87%D1%91%D1%82%D0%B0 (format, assignment at birth from 2020-07-15) ; https://buhexpert8.ru/voprosy/voprosy-1s-zup/snils-2.html
design_claims: SNILS as RU primary: no objection (universal from birth since 2020) ; encodes nothing: confirmed ; mod 101: confirmed at reference level (with the 100/101 -> 00 rule and the 001-001-998 exemption) ; safe = wrong check: confirmed
notes: Example verified with own script: 11223344595 passes, 11223344596 fails. The original PFR document (pfrf.ru/otchet_per/pravila_proverki_3.doc) is no longer online (PFR merged into SFR in 2023); evidence stays reference. python-stdnum has no SNILS module. Generator: draw the 9 digits above 001-001-998 and compute CC. A user forum (buhexpert8) reports a real number not matching the check: possibly early numbers or input errors, not used.

label: National ID number (MOI computer number)
structure: T (type: 1 = Saudi citizen; 2 = foreign resident (iqama); 3 or 5 = visitors incl. GCC citizens; 6 = pilgrims; 7 = government entities and companies) + NNNNNNNN (8-digit serial 00000000-99999999) + C (check derived from the other nine digits); 10 digits, no separators
encodes: citizen or resident (type digit) only
check: not published: SAMA's appendix says the formula is available from the MOI National Information Center on request. Third-party validators use Luhn over the 10 digits (double the digits in odd positions from the left, i.e. Luhn with the check last)
examples: 1012345672 (computed by me under the Luhn rule; citizen) ; 2012345670 (computed; resident) ; no authority-published example
assigned: at birth for citizens (the computer number given at birth becomes the national ID number); residents get it with the iqama
from_until: 10-digit computer number in use since at least the 1990s; no format change found
sources: https://rulebook.sama.gov.sa/en/entiresection/2324 (SAMA rulebook Appendix C: 'Explanation of the Combination of the Ten-Digit Computer Number of the Ministry of Interior') ; https://www.nuget.org/packages/SaudiIdValidator ; https://pypi.org/project/saudi-id-validator/1.0.4/ ; https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/sit-defn-saudi-arabia-national-id
design_claims: encodes citizen or resident: confirmed (issuer; types 3/5/6/7 also exist) ; Luhn: unconfirmed: the issuer withholds the formula; only third-party validators say Luhn ; safe = wrong check: confirmed with the caveat that a wrong-Luhn number is safe only if the real check is Luhn
notes: Evidence is issuer for the structure and the existence of a check digit, single (third-party validators) for Luhn. No published valid example to test Luhn against; the computed examples pass only by construction. In 1.0 generate type 1 for citizens (type 2 would be residents, out of scope). If the check is not Luhn, wrong_check numbers may collide with real ones; flag this in doc/data.md. The 'since the 1990s' start is my assumption, not sourced. ; [merge 2026-11-04] Weak: the check formula is unpublished (Luhn from third parties only); safe mode is not guaranteed.

label: Personal identity number
structure: YYMMDD (birth date) + '-' (born <100 years ago) or '+' (from the year the person turns 100) + NNN (födelsenummer 001-999, odd = male, even = female) + C (Luhn check over the 9 digits). Display YYMMDD-NNNC; electronic (Skatteverket ADB/Navet) form is 12 digits CCYYMMDDNNNC with century 18/19/20. Coordination number (samordningsnummer, since 2000) is the same with day + 60.
encodes: date, sex, century (separator in display form; explicit in 12-digit form); before 1990 the födelsenummer series was per county (län) of birth, from 1990 random from a national series
check: Luhn (mod 10, weights 2,1,2,... from the first of the 9 digits; digit-sum the products; check = (10 - sum mod 10) mod 10)
examples: 640823-3234 (man born 1964-08-23, födelsenummer 323; Skatteverket worked example, stored as 196408233234) ; 189001019802 (Skatteverket test personnummer, born 1890-01-01) ; 199308052381 (Skatteverket test personnummer, born 1993-08-05, female)
assigned: at birth registration in folkbokföring (or on immigration for those registered); current form with check digit from 1967, date + 3-digit birth number since 1947
safe_source: https://www.skatteverket.se/omoss/digitalasamarbeten/omvaraoppnadata/testpersonnummersomoppendata.4.5b35a6251761e6914202df9.html ; rowstore (JSON API, 43,895 rows, max 100 per page): https://skatteverket.entryscape.net/rowstore/dataset/b4de7df7-63c0-4e7e-bb59-1f156a591763 ; per-decade CSV files listed in https://skatteverket.entryscape.net/store/search?type=solr&query=public:true+AND+title:Testpersonnummer*
from_until: date + födelsenummer from 1947; check digit from 1967; county-based birth-number series until 1989, random national series from 1990; samordningsnummer from 2000
sources: https://docs.swedenconnect.se/technical-framework/mirror/skv/skv704-8.pdf ; https://www.skatteverket.se/privat/folkbokforing/personnummer ; https://sv.wikipedia.org/wiki/Personnummer_i_Sverige
design_claims: Skatteverket's published test numbers: confirmed (about 40,000 testpersonnummer + 2,000 testsamordningsnummer, open data on Skatteverket's Utvecklarportalen / EntryScape; Skatteverket blocks them so they are never assigned; new year's numbers added each December). Licence: none stated on the page; Skatteverket's open-data page says its open data is free to use with no agreement or fee
notes: Test numbers are not a simple range: sampled rows use födelsenummer 980-981 for births 1890-1905, 92x for some 1979-80 births and 238-239 for most other years, so safe mode must ship the list (or a year-indexed subset) rather than a rule. The open-data page says test numbers may carry risk if used in production. Examples checked with Luhn: 6408233234 pass, 9001019802 pass, 9308052381 pass, 6408233235 (altered) fails. Samordningsnummer (day+60) and the test samordningsnummer list are out of scope for 1.0. Licence of the test list should be confirmed with Skatteverket before redistribution (no explicit CC0 found).

label: NRIC number (UIN)
structure: P (prefix: S = citizens/PRs born before 2000, T = born 2000 on; F/G/M are foreigners' FINs, out of scope in 1.0) + NNNNNNN (7 digits; for citizens/PRs born 1968 on, the first two are the birth year, e.g. S71..., T02...; born before 1968: usually 0 or 1 by issue order, 2 or 3 for non-native residents) + L (checksum letter); 9 characters, e.g. S1234567D, same in display and electronic form
encodes: birth year (citizens and PRs born 1968 on), century (S/T prefix); FINs encode nothing
check: weights 2 7 6 5 4 3 2 on the 7 digits; add offset 0 for S/F, 4 for T/G, 3 for M; r = sum mod 11; letter = table[r] with S/T 'JZIHGFEDCBA', F/G 'XWUTRQPNMLK', M 'XWUTRQPNJLK' (index 0..10)
examples: S1234567D (common demonstration number, passes) ; T0212345I (computed by me: born 2002, passes) ; M1234567K (computed, passes under the M rule) ; note: M5678910B, the ICA example quoted by Forvis Mazars for the M series, does not pass the reverse-engineered M rule (it gives X), so it is illustrative only
assigned: at birth registration for Singapore-born citizens and PRs (the birth certificate number becomes the NRIC number); at PR/citizenship grant otherwise; card at 15
from_until: S series since 1965-67; birth-year digits for those born from 1968; T prefix for births from 2000-01-01; F before 2000, G 2000-2021, M from 2022-01-01 for FINs
sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Registration_Identity_Card (prefixes, birth-year rule; says the algorithm is not public and MHA sold it to approved organisations) ; https://www.ngiam.net/NRIC/NRIC_numbers.pdf (S/T/F/G weights, offset 4, tables) ; https://github.com/IonBazan/NRIC (M offset 3 and table XWUTRQPNJLK) ; https://userapps.support.sap.com/sap/support/knowledge/en/2572734 (SAP KBA: separate M table K L J N P Q R T U W X) ; https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/sit-defn-singapore-national-registration-identity-card-number
design_claims: encodes birth year (born 1968 on), century prefix: confirmed ; weighted letter: confirmed (reference; reverse-engineered, not published by ICA/MHA) ; S/T/F/G/M prefixes and the 2022 M series: confirmed (ICA via Forvis Mazars, Wikipedia) ; checksum letter tables: S/T and F/G confirmed (reference); M table and offset 3 single-source (one library plus a SAP KBA title), the ICA example M5678910B fails it ; safe = wrong letter: confirmed
notes: All computed examples pass my own code. Generation in 1.0 covers S/T only; for people born before 1968 draw a 0/1 first digit (not a birth year). FINs are random. Don't use the published early numbers of public figures.

label: unique master citizen number
structure: DD (day) + MM (month) + GGG (last three digits of birth year: 9xx = 19xx, 0xx = 20xx, 8xx = 18xx) + RR (register / registration-area code) + BBB (serial for people born the same day: 000-499 male, 500-999 female) + K (check). 13 digits, one block. Slovenia: RR = 50 (register code) for everyone until 2024; a ZCRP amendment (c. 2024) allows 51-59 when 50 is exhausted for a date (mostly foreigners registered on 1 January)
encodes: date, sex, century (3-digit year); RR is the Slovenian register code (50), not a birthplace
check: weights 7 6 5 4 3 2 7 6 5 4 3 2 on digits 1-12; r = sum mod 11; K = 11 - r; r = 0 gives K = 0; r = 1 (11 - r = 10) cannot give a digit, so that serial is skipped (BBB + 1) and the number is never assigned (Uredba 1999 art. 4)
examples: 2902932505526 (woman born 1932-02-29, register 50, serial 552; Uredba 1999 annex 1, invented example: weighted sum 192, remainder 5, K = 6) ; 0101006500006 (first boy registered on 2006-01-01; en/sl.wikipedia and python-stdnum) ; invalid: 0101006500007
assigned: at birth registration (Central Population Register, CRP); also given to foreigners resident in Slovenia
place_codes: Not a place code in Slovenia: 50 (51-59 as overflow from c. 2024). SFRJ-wide list (10-19 BA, 21-29 ME, 30-39 HR, 41-49 MK, 50 SI, 70-79 central RS, 80-89 Vojvodina, 91-96 Kosovo) on en.wikipedia citing Sl. list SFRJ 13/78; no Wikidata property found
from_until: JMBG from 1977-01-08 (Zakon o JMBG, Sl. list SFRJ 58/1976); Slovenian rules Uredba o nacinu dolocanja osebne identifikacijske stevilke, Ur. l. RS 8/1999 (ZCRP 1999); register codes 51-59 allowed by a ZCRP amendment around 2024 (exact date not verified)
sources: https://www.uradni-list.si/glasilo-uradni-list-rs/vsebina/1999-01-0345 (art. 3 structure, art. 4 check) ; https://sl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enotna_mati%C4%8Dna_%C5%A1tevilka_ob%C4%8Dana ; https://n1info.si/novice/slovenija/vlada-pripravila-zakon-ki-bo-spremenil-nove-emso/ (51-59) ; https://tax-fin-lex.si/Home/Novica/29334
design_claims: encodes date, sex, region: corrected: date, sex, century; the RR of Slovenian EMŠO is a register code (50, overflow 51-59), not a region ; mod 11: confirmed (weights 765432765432; r = 0 -> 0; r = 1 -> serial skipped, never assigned) ; safe = wrong check: confirmed
notes: Examples verified with own script: 2902932505526 and 0101006500006 pass, 0101006500007 fails. en.wikipedia states that m = 10 or 11 gives K = 0; the Slovenian Uredba (issuer) and sr.wikipedia say remainder 1 (m = 10) is skipped, so a generator must never emit r = 1 (then both readings accept it). Serbian/Bosnian/Montenegrin/Macedonian laws defer the algorithm to a bylaw. Foreigners: same structure (RR 50; SFRJ-era foreigner codes 00-09, 60-69), out of scope. Use RR = 50 for generated citizens.

label: birth number
structure: YYMMDD (birth date; MM = month for men, month + 50 for women) + NNNC (4-digit suffix incl. check) for people born from 1954-01-01, or NNN (3-digit suffix, no check) for people born up to 1953-12-31. 10-digit: YY 54-99 = 19YY, YY 00-53 = 20YY. Display form YYMMDD/NNNN, electronic form one block without the slash
encodes: date, sex, century (by length and YY)
check: the whole 10-digit number is divisible by 11. Historic exception: first 9 digits mod 11 = 10 gave C = 0 (ended 1985, shared with CZ). 9-digit numbers have no check
examples: 710319/2745 (male born 1971-03-19; python-stdnum sk.rc doctest) ; 736028/5163 (female 1973-10-28; cs.wikipedia, shared CS/SK format) ; invalid: 7103192746
assigned: at birth registration (Ministry of the Interior keeps the register, zakon 301/1995 Z. z. par. 3); foreigners on residence permit also
from_until: same Czechoslovak scheme since 1947 (vyhlaska 55/1976 Zb.); Slovak law 301/1995 Z. z. from 1996-01-01 (versions to 2024-07-15 keep the same par. 2); 9-digit before 1954. A meaningless replacement identifier (BIFO, random 10 digits) was approved by government in 2019 for 2020 with a 10-year transition; no evidence found that it replaced the rodné číslo
sources: https://static.slov-lex.sk/static/SK/ZZ/1995/301/20240715.html (par. 2 odst. 3-5) ; https://static.slov-lex.sk/static/SK/ZZ/1995/301/20220101.html (par. 8: change on sex change) ; https://www.oecd.org/content/dam/oecd/en/topics/policy-issue-focus/aeoi/slovak-republic-tin.pdf (month ranges 01-12 or 51-62) ; https://sk.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rodn%C3%A9_%C4%8D%C3%ADslo
design_claims: encodes date, sex (month + 50): confirmed ; +20/+70 extra series: corrected: Czech-only (CZ zakon 53/2004 Sb.); the Slovak law (version 2024-07-15) has only +50, and the Slovak Financial Administration's OECD sheet gives month ranges 01-12 or 51-62 only ; pre-1954 9-digit numbers: confirmed ; divisible by 11: confirmed ; remainder-10 exception: confirmed at reference level (sk.wikipedia, python-stdnum) ; safe = wrong check: confirmed
notes: Examples verified with own script: 7103192745 and 7360285163 pass, 7103192746 fails. No authority worked example found. Do not use +20/+70 months for SK (a CZ-born holder of a pre-1993 number may differ, out of scope). Number changes on sex change (par. 8). The Slovak law says 'up to 31 Dec 1953' 9 digits and 'after 1 Jan 1954' 10 digits. BIFO status after 2019 unverified.

label: Personal identification number
native_label: เลขประจำตัวประชาชน
structure: T (person type 1-8; 0 for people without registration status) + RRRR (registration office: province 2 digits + district/amphoe 2 digits; municipal offices count down from 99) + BBBBB (book/sequence within the office; for newborns the birth-certificate book) + NN (individual sequence) + C (check); 13 digits, display 1-2345-45678-78-1, electronic without dashes
encodes: category (type 1 = Thai born and registered on time, 2 = registered late, 3/4 = in house registers before 1984-05-31, 5 = added later, 6/7 = foreign residents and their children, 8 = naturalised), place (registration office of first registration; offices split after 1984 keep the parent's code for older numbers)
check: weights 13 12 11 10 9 8 7 6 5 4 3 2 on digits 1-12; x = sum mod 11; check = (11 - x) mod 10 (i.e. 1 - x when x <= 1)
examples: 3100600445635 (python-stdnum doctest, passes) ; 1-2345-45678-78-1 (python-stdnum doctest, passes) ; invalid: 1-2345-45678-78-9 (stdnum, wrong check)
assigned: at birth registration (type 1), from 1984-01-01; people already registered got type 3/4 numbers; ID card from age 7 (since the 2011 amendment)
place_codes: registration-office codes from the Department of Provincial Administration (DOPA); the first two digits are the province codes also used in ISO 3166-2:TH (e.g. 10 Bangkok). No official downloadable office list found in this survey; ISO 3166-2:TH via Wikidata P300 gives provinces only
sources: https://th.wikipedia.org/wiki/เลขประจำตัวประชาชนไทย (cites the Civil Registration Act B.E. 2534 s.16 and Ministerial Regulation No. 4 B.E. 2535) ; https://arthurdejong.org/python-stdnum/doc/stdnum.th.pin ; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thai_identity_card
design_claims: encodes category: corrected: category plus the registration office (province + district) of first registration ; weighted mod 11: confirmed ((11 - x) mod 10) ; safe = wrong check: confirmed
notes: Both stdnum examples pass my own code; the Thai Wikipedia illustration 1 1001 01245 29 9 fails (it is illustrative). For generation, type 1 for people born from 1984, type 3 for older people, office code from the province of birth/registration (place_source = registration). Numbers starting with 9 are reported as reserved for some royals (Thai Wikipedia).

label: Turkish identification number
structure: NNNNNNNNN (9 digits, first digit 1-9) + C1 + C2 (two check digits). 11 digits, one block
encodes: nothing
check: C1 = (7 x (d1+d3+d5+d7+d9) - (d2+d4+d6+d8)) mod 10 (equivalently 7 x odd-sum + 9 x even-sum mod 10); C2 = (d1+...+d9+C1) mod 10. Consequence: C2 = 8 x odd-sum mod 10, so the last digit is always even
examples: 17291716060 (python-stdnum doctest, not authority) ; invalid: 17291716050 (wrong check). No authority-published valid example found
assigned: at birth registration in MERNIS (Nüfus ve Vatandaşlık İşleri, NVI); all citizens numbered on introduction 2000-10-28
safe_source: https://www.turmob.org.tr/arsiv/mbs/resmigazete/-e-arsivkılavuz.pdf (GIB e-Arsiv guide: buyer TCKN may be given as 11111111111 when unknown; that placeholder fails the check, so it is not a structurally valid number)
from_until: since 2000-10-28 (MERNIS); used as the citizens' tax number since 2006-07-01 (OECD TIN sheet); format unchanged
sources: https://tr.wikipedia.org/wiki/T.C._Kimlik_Numaras%C4%B1 ; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turkish_Identification_Number ; python-stdnum stdnum/tr/tckimlik.py ; https://www.oecd.org/content/dam/oecd/en/topics/policy-issue-focus/aeoi/turkiye-tin.pdf (11 digits, TIN since 2006)
design_claims: encodes nothing: confirmed ; two digit rules: confirmed (C1 weighted 7/-1 mod 10, C2 digit sum mod 10; first digit non-zero) ; safe = wrong check: confirmed; no published test numbers found (GIB's 11111111111 and the unofficial 22222222222 are invoice placeholders and fail the check)
notes: Examples verified with own script: 17291716060 passes, 17291716050 fails; 11111111111 and 22222222222 fail. NVI publishes no algorithm; tr.wikipedia flags its own sources as unverified, but its rule, en.wikipedia and python-stdnum agree. A safe number via wrong check must keep the last digit even or odd consistently with the documented offset (any validator rejects it either way). Foreigners get a 'yabancı kimlik numarası' starting with 99, same check rules (not verified), out of scope. NVI's KPS SOAP service checks real numbers, never call it.

label: National identification number
structure: L (letter: municipality/county of first household registration) + S (1 = male, 2 = female) + N (third digit: 0-5 Taiwan-born; 6 naturalised ex-foreigner; 7 naturalised without prior household registration; 8 from Hong Kong/Macau; 9 from mainland China, since 2003-07-01; before that part of the serial) + NNNNNN (serial) + C (check); 10 characters, e.g. A123456789, same in display and electronic form
encodes: place (county/city of first household registration; letter kept when boundaries change), sex; third digit: origin category since 2003
check: letter -> two digits (A10 B11 C12 D13 E14 F15 G16 H17 I34 J18 K19 L20 M21 N22 O35 P23 Q24 R25 S26 T27 U28 V29 W32 X30 Y31 Z33); weights 1 9 on the letter's two digits, then 8 7 6 5 4 3 2 1 on digits 2-9 and 1 on the check; valid when the sum is divisible by 10 (check = (10 - partial sum mod 10) mod 10)
examples: A123456789 (Taipei City, male; the widely used demonstration number, passes) ; no authority-published example found
assigned: at first household registration (birth registration); naturalised citizens at registration
place_codes: 26 letters in Article 5 of the MOI regulation; current: A Taipei, B Taichung, C Keelung, D Tainan, E Kaohsiung, F New Taipei, G Yilan, H Taoyuan, I Chiayi City, J Hsinchu County, K Miaoli, M Nantou, N Changhua, O Hsinchu City, P Yunlin, Q Chiayi County, T Pingtung, U Hualien, V Taitung, W Kinmen, X Penghu, Z Lienchiang; discontinued: L Taichung County, R Tainan County, S Kaohsiung County (2010 mergers), Y Yangmingshan (1974). I and O used only after 1982 (per zh.wikipedia). Small enough to curate; no Wikidata property needed
from_until: 10-character form with check since 1969 (zh.wikipedia); third-digit category since 2003-07-01; letters L/R/S stopped for new registrations after the 2010-12-25 mergers. Foreign residents' UI numbers adopted the same shape with second digit 8/9 from 2021-01-02 (out of scope)
sources: https://law.moj.gov.tw/LawClass/LawAll.aspx?PCode=D0030030 (國民身分證及戶口名簿製發相片影像檔建置管理辦法, Art. 5: 10 characters, first letter = municipality/county, second digit sex code, tenth check code) ; https://zh.wikipedia.org/zh-tw/中華民國國民身分證 (letter values and check formula) ; https://docs.rs/tw-id-num
design_claims: encodes county of first registration, sex: confirmed (plus an origin category in the third digit since 2003) ; weighted mod 10: confirmed ; safe = wrong check: confirmed
notes: Structure is issuer-level (Art. 5 of the MOI regulation); the check formula itself was found only in Wikipedia and programming write-ups (an Executive Yuan gazette attachment is cited by blogs but I could not open it), hence reference. A123456789 passes my own check code. Generation: draw letters among the current 22 for people registered after 2010, include L/R/S/Y by era for older people; third digit 0-5 for Taiwan-born.

label: taxpayer registration card number
native_label: реєстраційний номер облікової картки платника податків (РНОКПП)
structure: XXXXX (sequence number of the birth date: usually the number of days from 1899-12-31 to the birth date, so 00001 = 1900-01-01; the State Tax Service says one birth date can have two or more such numbers) + NNNN (sequence number of the account card; its last digit, the 9th, is odd = male, even = female) + K (check). 10 digits, one block
encodes: date (day count), sex
check: weights -1 5 7 9 4 6 10 5 7 on digits 1-9; K = (sum mod 11) mod 10, with a non-negative modulo (remainder 10 gives 0)
examples: 1759013776 (python-stdnum doctest; decodes to 1948-02-28 by day count, 9th digit 7 = male) ; 2530414071 (python-stdnum format doctest; 1969-04-12, 9th digit 7 = male) ; invalid: 1759013770. No authority-published example found
assigned: on registration in the State Register of Individuals-Taxpayers (DRFO), at the tax office of residence on application (form 1DR) or through the Diia 'eMalyatko' birth-registration bundle (not verified); persons with religious objections may refuse it and use their passport instead
from_until: from 1994-1995 (law 320/94-VR of 1994-12-22, DRFO; then 'identification code'); renamed RNOKPP under the Tax Code (2010); current registration rules MinFin order 822 of 2017-09-29
sources: https://www.oecd.org/content/dam/oecd/en/topics/policy-issue-focus/aeoi/ukraine-tin.pdf (State Tax Service: XXXXX birth-date sequence, NNNN card sequence, K control; algorithm 'determined by the STS') ; https://uk.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D0%A0%D0%B5%D1%94%D1%81%D1%82%D1%80%D0%B0%D1%86%D1%96%D0%B9%D0%BD%D0%B8%D0%B9_%D0%BD%D0%BE%D0%BC%D0%B5%D1%80_%D0%BE%D0%B1%D0%BB%D1%96%D0%BA%D0%BE%D0%B2%D0%BE%D1%97_%D0%BA%D0%B0%D1%80%D1%82%D0%BA%D0%B8_%D0%BF%D0%BB%D0%B0%D1%82%D0%BD%D0%B8%D0%BA%D0%B0_%D0%BF%D0%BE%D0%B4%D0%B0%D1%82%D0%BA%D1%96%D0%B2 (day count from 1899-12-31, sex digit, weights) ; python-stdnum stdnum/ua/rntrc.py
design_claims: days since 1899-12-31: confirmed at reference level (uk.wikipedia says 'usually'; the issuer only says 'sequence number of registration of birth date' and that one date can have several values, e.g. 1947-01-01 numbers starting with 1 or 8) ; sex digit: confirmed at reference level (9th digit odd = male, even = female) ; weighted mod 11: confirmed (weights -1 5 7 9 4 6 10 5 7, mod 11 then mod 10) ; safe = wrong check: confirmed
notes: Examples verified with own script: 1759013776 and 2530414071 pass, 1759013770 fails. python-stdnum checks only the check digit, not the date. Generator: use the day count (the usual case); note that the alternative leading values for some dates are undocumented. Implementations must use a non-negative modulo (the weighted sum can be negative because of the -1 weight). Foreigners get the same format, out of scope.

label: Social Security number
structure: AAA (area, 3 digits) + GG (group, 2 digits) + SSSS (serial, 4 digits). Display AAA-GG-SSSS, electronic 9 digits. Area 000, 666 and 900-999 never assigned; group 00 and serial 0000 never valid. Before 2011-06-25: area = state of the mailing address on the application (SSA area-by-state table); group issued within each area in the order odd 01-09, even 10-98, even 02-08, odd 11-99; serial 0001-9999 sequential within group. From 2011-06-25: area, group and serial random over all permitted values
encodes: before 2011-06-25: place (state of the mailing address on the application, not birth) via area, and issue period via group (sequence); from 2011-06-25: nothing
check: none
examples: no check digit, so no worked examples; SSA publishes none. Invalid by rule (SSA randomization FAQ): any 000-GG-SSSS, 666-GG-SSSS, 9XX-GG-SSSS, AAA-00-SSSS, AAA-GG-0000 ; 987-65-4320 to 987-65-4329 are commonly called the advertising numbers (HUD lists 987-65-4320 among numbers printed in advertising), but no SSA source for the reservation was found
assigned: on application (Form SS-5), from 1936; children mostly at birth through Enumeration at Birth (hospital birth registration, since 1987) — EAB date from SSA Bulletin v69n2, not re-verified this session
place_codes: area-by-state table: SSA 'Social Security Number Allocations' (ssa.gov/employer/stateweb.htm) and SSA Bulletin v45n11 (1982) Table 1; high group lists: SSA monthly 'High Group List', final edition 'HIGHEST GROUP ISSUED AS OF 06/24/11' still at ssa.gov/employer/ssns/highgroup.txt, earlier monthly editions archived by UNT web archive (webarchive.library.unt.edu/eot2008/.../ssnvhighgroup.htm) and the Internet Archive. US federal works, public domain (17 U.S.C. 105). Wikidata: no property for SSN areas found
safe_source: https://www.ssa.gov/employer/randomizationfaqs.html (randomization 'introduced previously unassigned area numbers for assignment excluding area numbers 000, 666 and 900-999'; group 00 and serial 0000 'will continue to be invalid')
from_until: from 1936 (first numbers); geographic area + sequential group until 2011-06-24; random assignment from 2011-06-25 (existing numbers unchanged, both kinds held by living people)
sources: https://www.ssa.gov/employer/randomizationfaqs.html ; https://www.ssa.gov/employer/randomization.html ; https://www.ssa.gov/employer/ssnweb.htm (group order: 'ODD numbers from 01 through 09 and then EVEN numbers from 10 through 98 ... followed by EVEN 02-08 and ODD 11-99') ; https://ssa.gov/employer/ssnvhighgroup.htm (final High Group List) ; https://www.ssa.gov/policy/docs/ssb/v45n11/v45n11p29.pdf ; https://www.ssa.gov/policy/docs/ssb/v69n2/v69n2p55.html
design_claims: areas 000, 666, 900-999 never issued: confirmed (SSA randomization FAQ) ; safe = areas 000 and 666: confirmed, and group 00 / serial 0000 are also never valid ; group order odd 01-09, even 10-98, even 02-08, odd 11-99: confirmed (SSA ssnweb.htm) ; randomisation from 2011-06-25: confirmed ; area-by-state table and high group lists archived and public domain: confirmed (ssa.gov stateweb.htm, final highgroup.txt of 2011-06-24, UNT/Internet Archive monthly copies; 17 U.S.C. 105) ; 'state of issue': corrected: the area followed the state of the mailing address on the SS-5 application (since 1972 assigned centrally), not birth state ; [merge 2026-11-04] Area = state of the issuing office before 1972, ZIP code of the mailing address from 1972 (ssa.gov/history/ssn/geocard.html).
notes: ssa.gov returns 403 to scripts and the Internet Archive throttled (429), so SSA page wording was taken from search-result quotes of ssa.gov pages; the area-by-state table itself was not downloaded this session. Do not draw safe numbers from 900-999: IRS ITINs are 9XX with group 50-65, 70-88, 90-92, 94-99 and are held by real people (987-65-432x has group 65, ITIN-shaped). Some area ranges (e.g. 700-728 railroad, 729-733 enumeration, 580 territories) are not states; Puerto Rico, Guam etc. have areas. Group numbers per area did not advance uniformly, so series.tsv anchors are per area. No SSN examples to verify (no check digit)

label: Identity card number
native_label: Número de cédula de identidad (C.I.) / documento de identidad
structure: N.NNN.NNN (up to 7 digits; 6-digit numbers are left-padded with 0 for the check) + '-' + C (check digit). Display N.NNN.NNN-C, electronic 8 digits
encodes: nothing found; assignment order not documented
check: weighted mod 10: digits 1-7 times 2,9,8,7,6,3,4; s = sum; C = (10 - s mod 10) mod 10
examples: 1.234.567-2 (hacecuentas.com worked example: sum 148, remainder 8, check 2; third party) ; the Revista Pensamiento Matemático article (2018) works the rule on the author's own number, not recorded here ; no authority example found
assigned: by the Dirección Nacional de Identificación Civil (DNIC); the card is compulsory from 45 days of age (es.wikipedia)
from_until: current 7+1 digit format; electronic card ('documento de identidad') from 2015-05 keeps the number; start date of the numbering not found
sources: https://documat.unirioja.es/descarga/articulo/6636701.pdf (Revista Pensamiento Matemático VIII-2, 2018: control number 2987634) ; https://hacecuentas.com/uy/validar-cedula ; https://pypi.org/project/cedula-uruguaya/ ; https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9dula_de_identidad_(Uruguay) ; https://www.elobservador.com.uy/ciencia-y-tecnologia/denuncian-que-se-pueden-crear-usuarios-cedulas-ficticias-que-impacto-tiene-el-estado-n6025776
design_claims: sequential (survey): unconfirmed: no DNIC or other source on how numbers are assigned was found; the 2018 article says only that DNIC assigns the numbers ; weighted mod 10 with weights 2987634: confirmed (reference: math journal article + third-party validators; El Observador 2025 reports gub.uy itself validates only the check digit; no DNIC/AGESIC text of the algorithm found)
notes: python-stdnum has no Uruguayan cédula module (only stdnum.uy.rut). Own check: 1234567 -> 2 (pass). Foreign residents get a cédula too (yellow card, 'Extranjero'); their numbering is not documented. Without a sourced sequence, draw uniformly over 1.000.000-6.999.999 or similar, and say it is a design choice

label: Personal identification number (citizen ID card number)
native_label: Số định danh cá nhân (số căn cước / căn cước công dân)
structure: PPP (province code where the birth was registered, or a country code for births registered abroad) + G (century and sex: 0/1 = 1900s male/female, 2/3 = 2000s, 4/5 = 2100s, 6/7 = 2200s, 8/9 = 2300s) + YY (last two digits of the birth year) + NNNNNN (random); 12 digits, no separators
encodes: place (province of birth registration), century, sex, year
check: none
examples: 012198123456 (LuatVietnam example: province code 012, female, born 1998) ; no second authority example found
assigned: at birth registration (số định danh cá nhân, set up in the national population database); the 12-digit card number equals it; card from age 14 (from birth on request since 2024)
place_codes: Province codes: Circular 59/2021/TT-BCA Art. 4 cl. 1, Appendix I (province codes) and Appendix II (country codes for births abroad), earlier Circular 07/2016/TT-BCA Appendix I; the 63 province codes are 001-096 = '0' + the GSO 2-digit administrative code (e.g. 001 Ha Noi, 002 Ha Giang, 031 Hai Phong, 048 Da Nang, 079 Ho Chi Minh City, 092 Can Tho). Since 2024-07-01 the Law on Identification 2023 and Decree 70/2024/ND-CP (replacing Decree 137/2015) apply, with Circular 17/2024/TT-BCA (amended by 53/2025 and 118/2026). Wikidata P14879 (Vietnamese administrative unit code) has only 35 items (the post-2025 provinces), so old provinces are not covered there; use the GSO 2004 list (Decision 124/2004/QD-TTg)
from_until: 12-digit number since 2016 (Decree 137/2015, Circular 07/2016); 9-digit CMND numbers held by older people until replaced (CMND invalid from 2025-01-01). 2025-07-01: 63 provinces merged into 34 (Resolution 202/2025/QH15; new administrative codes in Decision 19/2025/QD-TTg); issued numbers are lifelong and do not change
sources: https://caselaw.vn/van-ban-phap-luat/363143-thong-tu-so-59-2021-tt-bca-ngay-15-05-2021-cua-bo-truong-bo-cong-an-huong-dan-luat-can-cuoc-cong-dan-va-nghi-dinh-137-2015-nd-cp-huong-dan-luat-can-cuoc-cong-dan-sua-doi-bang-nghi-dinh-37-2021-nd-cp (Art. 4: codes in Appendices I-III) ; https://luatvietnam.vn/hanh-chinh/nhin-so-can-cuoc-cong-dan-de-biet-nam-sinh-570-97055-article.html (Decree 137/2015 Art. 13 structure, century/sex table, province codes) ; https://baolaocai.vn/thong-tin-trong-can-cuoc-dieu-chinh-ra-sao-khi-sap-xep-con-34-tinh-thanh-post403558.html
design_claims: encodes province, century, sex, year: confirmed ; check none: confirmed ; province codes source: confirmed: Circular 59/2021/TT-BCA Appendix I (before: 07/2016), codes = '0' + GSO code ; century+sex digit and year: confirmed ; 2025 mergers 63 -> 34: confirmed that issued numbers and cards stay valid; unconfirmed whether newborns registered after 2025-07-01 get the 34 new codes (no circular found that amends the code appendix) ; unassigned province code: corrected: gaps exist in the 63-code list (e.g. 003, 005, 007, 009, 013), but Appendix II country codes for births abroad share the same 3-digit space and I could not read that appendix, so an unassigned code is not proven; keep unassigned_place only after checking Appendix II, else use an impossible year/century combination
notes: I could not read Appendices I-III themselves (paywalled/login), so the code list is reference-level (LuatVietnam reproduction). If the new 34-province codes follow Decision 19/2025 (each kept one merging province's GSO code, e.g. Lao Cai 15, Thai Nguyen 19), they are a subset of the old codes and the old-code table still covers them. Birth-year rule: century digit and YY together give the full year, so an 'impossible' safe number could use a birth year after the reference date. The CMND end date (2025-01-01) is from the Law on Identification 2023 as I know it, not re-verified here. ; [merge 2026-11-04] safe_method set to impossible_date until Appendix II (codes for births abroad) of Circular 59/2021 is read; unassigned_place is unproven.

label: Identity number
structure: YYMMDD (birth date, no century indicator) + SSSS (sequence: 0000-4999 female, 5000-9999 male) + C (status: 0 citizen, 1 permanent resident, 2 refugee) + A (8 or 9; formerly a race identifier, now random) + Z (Luhn check). Display YYMMDD SSSS CAZ (often without spaces), electronic 13 digits
encodes: date of birth (century not encoded), sex (sequence range), citizenship status
check: Luhn over all 13 digits
examples: 7503305044089 (python-stdnum: born 1975-03-30, male (5044), citizen (0), A 8) ; invalid: 8503305044089 (stdnum). No authority example found
assigned: at birth registration with the Department of Home Affairs (population register); identity document/smart ID card from age 16 — not re-verified this session
from_until: 13-digit format under the Identification Act 68 of 1997 s. 7 (date of birth, gender, citizenship 'in figure codes') and its predecessors (Population Registration Act era); A digit was a race code before it became 8/9 (date of change not sourced here)
sources: https://www.irb-cisr.gc.ca/en/country-information/rir/Pages/index.aspx?doc=454798 (IRB Canada RIR ZAF104570.E, 2013-09-13, quoting the Identification Act 1997 s. 7 and Lawyers for Human Rights) ; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_African_identity_card ; https://arthurdejong.org/python-stdnum/doc/2.1/stdnum.za.idnr
design_claims: encodes date, sex, citizenship: confirmed (Identification Act 1997 s. 7 via IRB Canada; digit values reference-level) ; Luhn: confirmed (reference: Wikipedia + stdnum; DHA publishes no algorithm text found) ; safe = wrong check: confirmed
notes: Own check: 7503305044089 pass, 8503305044089 fail. A change of status (permanent resident to citizen) or of sex gives a new number (IRB RIR). Two-digit year: numbers are not unique across centuries. dha.gov.za not reachable in search results; status 2 (refugee) is from LHR via IRB, not DHA. Generate A = 8 for modern numbers

label: National identity card number
structure: three forms in circulation: 13 digits (2008 card): DD (district) + R (RMO code) + UU (upazila) + WW (union/ward) + NNNNNN (personal number); 17 digits: YYYY (birth year) + the same 13 digits; 10 digits (smart card, from 2016): 9 random digits + 1 checksum digit, first digit not 0, no digit four or more times, no digit three times in a row, no sequences
encodes: 13/17-digit: place (district, RMO, upazila, union/ward, BBS geocodes) and, in the 17-digit form, birth year; 10-digit: nothing
check: 13/17-digit: none found; 10-digit: a checksum digit exists (EC decision 2015) but its algorithm is not published
examples: none published
assigned: at voter registration (18+) for the 13-digit 2008 card; birth registration numbers (17 digits) are a different scheme
place_codes: BBS (Bangladesh Bureau of Statistics) geocodes, 2 digits per level (per a government form)
from_until: 13-digit from 2008; 17-digit for later registrations/updates; 10-digit smart-card numbers adopted 2015 (issued from 2016)
sources: https://bdnews24.com/bangladesh/election-commission-decides-on-10-digit-smart-nid-cards-for-bangladesh-nationals (2015-06-23: 10 digits, 9 random + checksum, rules) ; https://m.somewhereinblog.net/mobile/blog/tanjid/29980228 (2014 blog: 13/17-digit segments) ; https://docs.signzy.com/us-apis/bangladesh-nid-verification (10/13/17 lengths) ; https://shed.gov.bd//sites/default/files/files/shed.portal.gov.bd/notices/8192af5f_97f4_4696_8b97_94384bf1ee26/ilovepdf_merged%20(1).pdf (BBS 2-digit district/upazila codes)
design_claims: unserved: corrected: the 13/17-digit forms have a reported structure (birth year + BBS place codes + serial, no check; single blog source), and the 10-digit smart-card number has a checksum digit whose algorithm is unpublished; nothing at issuer level, so staying unserved in 1.0 is right
notes: If served later, the 17-digit form (birth year + place) is the only decodable one, but its segment layout rests on a 2014 blog. The 10-digit form's checksum rule must not be guessed.

label: Unique Personal Identification Number (citizenship card number)
native_label: Número Único de Identificación Personal (NUIP) / número de cédula de ciudadanía
structure: since Resolución 3571 of 2003-09-30 (Diario Oficial 45.327, 2003-10-01): 10 digits starting at 1.000.000.000; 1.000.000.000-1.009.999.999 reserved for equivalences of the 2000-2003 alphanumeric NUIPs; people with a cédula before 2003 keep the cédula number as NUIP (shorter numbers); minors with an 11-digit NIP keep it on the tarjeta de identidad until adulthood. Numeric blocks ('cupos') are allocated to each registry office by Registraduría resolutions
encodes: sequence within the block allocated to the registering office (so the office of registration, indirectly); no check digit
check: none
assigned: at birth registration or when applying for the cédula (Resolución 6801 of 2013)
place_codes: office codes and number blocks published one by one in Registraduría resolutions (Cancillería normograma, vLex); no consolidated list found
from_until: 10-digit NUIP from 2003-10; alphanumeric NUIP 2000-2003 (Res. 0146/2000, first 3 characters = registry office); older cédula numbers retained
sources: https://www.cancilleria.gov.co/sites/default/files/Normograma/docs/pdf/resolucion_registraduria_3571_2003.pdf ; https://cancilleria.gov.co/sites/default/files/Normograma/docs/resolucion_registraduria_6801_2013.htm ; https://cancilleria.gov.co/normograma/compilacion/docs/resolucion_registraduria_0146_2000.htm
design_claims: unserved: corrected: the structure is published (Res. 3571/2003: 10 digits from 1.000.000.000, a reserved equivalence block 1.000.000.000-1.009.999.999, office blocks by resolution); there is still no check digit, so it stays unserved under decision 2 unless that decision admits sequential numbers without a check
notes: The equivalence block is not 'never issued' (it holds converted NUIPs). Resolution texts were read only through search excerpts; confirm the full Res. 3571 text before relying on details

label: National ID number
structure: 14 digits: C (century: 2 = 1900s, 3 = 2000s) + YYMMDD (birth date) + GG (governorate code: 01-04, 11-19, 21-29, 31-35, 88 abroad per django-localflavor) + NNNN (sequence; the second-to-last digit odd = male, even = female) + K (check digit)
encodes: date of birth, century, governorate of birth, sex
check: unknown: no official algorithm; one Rust crate implements Luhn over 13 digits, another package calls its checksum 'private'
assigned: birth registration (Civil Status Organization) - not verified
